chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Songwriting for Robbins after Boston
summary: McRae stayed in New York writing for the Robbins staff, including "Santa Rosa" and "I'm Afraid of Love".

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: -- after -- goes into that rock and roll (this inaudible) that I gave you. This is in the 50's -- 40's.

When I came back from Boston, what I just started doing -- I didn't do any gigging around in Boston. Most a lot of musicians come in, they want to start doing some gigging (inaudible). I had some other writing to do for Robbins at that time, you know. (Inaudible). Then (inaudible) the things that I had over there. I did -- was a very good writer -- I did a thing called "Santa Rosa." It was a latin type of thing that we did. One of the top writers over there, I did that. I'll give you --
Yeah. Well I was writing on the staff, so I could write with anybody. You know, like you become
